overview: The two halves of the ovarian cycle, split by ovulation, each dominated by a different hormone.
genZNote: Follicular phase: the build-up before the big event. Luteal phase: what happens after, corpus luteum in charge.

aspects.label: Dominant Hormone
aspects.valueA: Estrogen, rising as the follicle matures.
aspects.valueB: Progesterone, secreted by the corpus luteum.

aspects.label: Main Event
aspects.valueA: Growth and maturation of an ovarian follicle, ending in ovulation.
aspects.valueB: Formation and function of the corpus luteum, preparing the endometrium for possible implantation.

aspects.label: Cycle-Length Variability
aspects.valueA: Variable in length — mainly responsible for differences in overall cycle length between people.
aspects.valueB: Relatively fixed in length (~14 days), regardless of total cycle length.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: The luteal phase length is remarkably consistent (~14 days) across people, while the follicular phase is what actually varies cycle length.
overlay.memoryTrick: Follicular = before ovulation, follicle growing. Luteal = after ovulation, corpus luteum active.
overlay.commonMisconception: Ovulation is not part of either phase — it's the dividing event between the follicular and luteal phases.
